The 3pm blackout has existed in English football since the 1960s

After 60 years, is time finally running out on the 3pm blackout in football?

With pretty much every available television slot now exhausted, next year the Premier League and the EFL are set to hold serious discussions about its future.

There are concerns, especially within non-league football, that removing the blackout could have detrimental effects on attendances and finances.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham agrees, urging caution and suggesting the health of the football pyramid should come first .

But many Premier League fans feel they are short-changed, locked out of many of their team's fixtures just because they live in this country.

Go anywhere else in the world, and every single match is available live.

With streaming so prevalent, to some the blackout feels archaic.

Yet it is a complex situation, and many feel the depth of English football's pyramid is like nowhere else.

BBC Sport looks at the history of the blackout, why it is unique to British football and the arguments for and against keeping it.

It is the start of the 1964-65 season and the BBC launches a programme called Match of the Day .

Highlights of one match would be broadcast on BBC Two, a channel which at the time was only available in London.

Yet some clubs were concerned. Would fans still turn up to games?

Burnley chairman Bob Lord was the first owner to refuse to allow the cameras into Turf Moor. At the end of the season, several other clubs tried to block the renewal of the deal.

A compromise was reached and the BBC agreed not to reveal the televised Saturday match until all games had ended.

Shortly afterwards came the blackout for live matches.

Fast forward 20 years to 1987. With dwindling attendances across the European domestic leagues, partly influenced by crowd trouble, Uefa took up England's idea.

Article 48 was added to the Uefa Statutes.

Each country could designate a two-and-a-half-hour "transmission-free period", as long as at least 50% of matches in the top two leagues were taking place.

This was "designed to ensure that spectators are not deterred from attending local football matches of any kind and/or participating in matches at amateur and/or youth level".

Today, the situation has gone full circle. The only leagues that apply Article 48 are England, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

The reason for this is simpler than you might imagine.

No other major country qualifies for the blackout - because no other major country has a kick-off time that runs from the top flight and through the divisions.

It is a tradition that is unique to football in the United Kingdom.

Let's take Germany, often held up as an example of a country with excellent attendances despite not having a blackout.

This misses a key point. The Bundesliga has its own kick-off slot, 3:30pm on a Saturday, and no other division plays at the same time. The 2. Bundesliga, for instance, has a standard Saturday kick-off time of 1:30pm.

Could you imagine English football replicating this?

In Spain, it is rare for either of the top two divisions to have games that kick off simultaneously. Each match has its own slot, and is broadcast live.

In Italy, Serie A plays on a Sunday afternoon, and Serie B on a Saturday.

In France, Ligue 1 has Saturday night as its main time slot, Ligue 2 plays largely on a Friday night, and Ligue 3 on a Saturday lunchtime.

So there is no blackout, because the football calendar works in a completely different way.

Football fans give their thoughts on the Saturday 3pm TV blackout

The next television rights cycle presents a unique opportunity.

The deals for the Premier League, EFL and Scottish Premiership are all up for renewal in 2029-30.

There is the chance for all the top stakeholders to come together and agree to end the blackout.

Last year, Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said there were no plans to remove the blackout.

But this summer there was a clear shift in emphasis, with Masters admitting there would be talks with the EFL ahead of the renewal of TV rights.

Scottish football has gone first, with broadcasters invited to bid to show all matches live - and is open to those shown on a Saturday afternoon .

It will be another year before we discover what the Premier League and the EFL - which seriously considered ending the blackout three years ago - are prepared to offer to broadcasters.

So, why would the leagues need to offer up the Saturday 3pm slot to broadcasters? After all, the latest domestic Premier League deal was worth a record £6.7bn - an increase of 4%.

However, to achieve that figure, the Premier League had to make an additional 70 games available. In real terms, it means each live Premier League game is worth less than it was before.

Now every single game not shown at 3pm on a Saturday - and there are only 110 left - is on TV.

Could the Premier League need to offer more matches for the rights to keep their overall value?

If so there are two options: try to find more TV slots, or show games at 3pm on a Saturday.

Could the Women's Super League benefit too? It looked into playing a 3pm on a Saturday but could not find a way around the blackout.

Most of the competition's games are shown live already, with a greater concern being stadium availability and consistency of kick-off times.

There is a danger that the issue of the 3pm blackout is viewed only through the lens of Premier League and EFL television rights.

Tom Greatrex, the chair of the Football Supporters' Association, says there are attendances in non-league football that some top flights in Europe "would look at jealously".

"We have one of the strongest football pyramids in the world, with excellent matchday attendances deep into the non-league game," Greatrex said.

"The prime minister is right to point out the value of the blackout to clubs further down the pyramid, and to urge caution over the impact rushed change could have on the overall health of the game."

BBC Sport understands that senior executives at the National League, which has a long-term global streaming deal with DAZN, are steadfastly against the blackout ending.

It has serious reservations, shared by the vast majority of its 72 clubs, that attendances would be impacted.

Included in this is transient attendance from season ticket holders of league clubs, who attend non-league football when their team is away from home, boosting receipts considerably.

The fear is this could be lost if all league games are streamed at 3pm.

Nicky Bloom, the chair of Northern Premier League side FC United of Manchester, worries that the issue is only viewed through the lens of top-flight football.

"Football doesn't begin and end with the Premier League," Bloom told BBC Sport.

"Every Saturday, thousands of people turn out to support their local clubs.

"For many of those clubs, the income from people coming through the turnstiles, buying a pint or something to eat is what keeps them alive.

"The 3pm blackout isn't about nostalgia. It's about protecting something that matters."

Bloom added that clubs in non-league football are huge community assets, and losing them would have an impact "well beyond 90 minutes on a Saturday".

Some clubs are more open-minded about what ending the blackout could mean for non-league football.

Others have changed the way they operate to get around it.

North West Counties League Premier Division side FC Isle of Man have stopped playing at 3:00pm on a Saturday so they can stream all their games live.

Brian Shotton, a director at eighth-tier Ashington FC, told BBC Sport that he would not be automatically against removing the blackout.

"I would still have concerns, because every person through the gate makes a difference," Shotton said.

"I don't think we should just assume it would damage non-league football, but equally you need to know what it could mean for clubs like ours."

Ashington, which have attendances of about 400, see gates rise by up to 25% when Newcastle are not at home - but they already see the impact of illegal streaming of the Magpies' games.

For the official broadcasters like Sky Sports, these supporters are seen as lost revenue.

There is an argument that the blackout drives piracy. Just how many of those particular fans would pay for a legal subscription is open to debate.

Added to that, there are now many weekends when when fewer than 50% of matches in the top two divisions are played at 3pm on a Saturday anyway.

For instance, on 28 November there are just two in the Premier League, and seven in the Championship.

Other non-league clubs, like Dorking Wanders and Hashtag United, have spoken of the opportunities ending the blackout could bring, such as more income streams and fewer inconvenient kick-off times.

But this, for now, seems to be a minority view. The concerns for the health of the entire pyramid, on attendances and finances, are real.

Once the blackout is gone, it is unlikely to come back.

Ashley Jensen will return for the 12th series of Shetland to be filmed next year

The BBC detective drama Shetland is to return for a 12th series, with filming starting next year.

The new six-part series will see the return of Ashley Jensen, playing DI Ruth Calder, and longstanding cast members Steven Robertson as DS Sandy Wilson and Lewis Howden as PC Billy McCabe.

But DI Tosh McIntosh will be a notable absence because one of the original stars, Alison O'Donnell, leaves the drama at the end of the current series following a 13-year stint.

Further casting details for the next series will be announced in due course.

The show, filmed both in Shetland and at locations in mainland Scotland, averaged seven million viewers across 2025.

Anita Vettesse will take over as lead writer on the new series, which will be produced by Angus Sharpe and distributed internationally by ITV Studios.

The TV series, adapted from the novels by Ann Cleeves, was first broadcast on BBC One in March 2013.

DI Jimmy Perez, played by Douglas Henshall, was the central character for the first seven series, with Ashley Jensen then joining as DI Calder in 2023.

Watch: Marco Rubio says recent tech outages are 'completely unrelated' to one another

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed widespread concerns online that the series of recent tech outages in the past week are connected, telling reporters there was "zero evidence" of any link.

Rubio acknowledged that "people are fearful" the spate of outages, which included all flights being grounded in the US and widespread disruptions to banking, Apple and Microsoft services, could be linked or part of a plot.

"We are not under systemic attack," he said. "These events, one has nothing to do with the other, they are not inter-related."

Cyber-security experts have agreed that there is no evidence linking the outages, and many of the issues appear due to updates to old infrastructure.

In the past week, there has been a massive Microsoft outage , an apparent tech glitch which grounded all US flights for hours, and issues for the National Security Agency, outages affecting the biggest US banks and Apple.

Every affected company or agency has said the issue was not cyber-related and not the work of an outside actor.

Rubio's comments came hours after US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton also addressed the issue, telling Fox News the outages were not the product of a cyber-attack. He explained "lots of institutions" are patching or upgrading systems, which has caused some disruption.

Rubio was asked whether the Trump administration was concerned public fears could lead to stockpiling or a run on the banks.

He said the best way to combat such fears was for the US government to share everything they know with the American people.

"Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause that has nothing to do with a cyber-criminal, has nothing to do with a hostile actor or another country," he said.

Technology-related disruptions have happened almost daily since Thursday, when a Microsoft outage disrupted many of its services, including email.

The next day, the US Federal Aviation Administration halted flights across the US for more than four hours with a rare national ground stop. It was the longest halting of flights since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US.

The US transport secretary said the issue was technical and caused by a copper wire upgrade and outdated equipment.

On Monday, a United Airlines technology failure delayed about 150 flights and a JPMorgan Chase software problem disrupted service at the biggest and most utilised banks in the US.

Both United and Chase said a software issue was behind the glitch.

Apple users were impacted by outages affecting iCloud and Apple Pay on Tuesday. The company said the cause was not a cyber-attack but the outage was triggered by an an internal update.

The same day, a highly classified network used by the US National Security Agency (NSA) for internal communications also went offline for a period of time.

Passengers wait to check in at Los Angeles International Airport as flights resume after being grounded for several hours on November 13 due to a major communications outage.

Cybersecurity experts say there is no evidence connecting the Microsoft, airline, and bank disruptions from the last five days.

Kris Beevers, CEO and co-founder of the network and infrastructure management company NetBox Labs, acknowledged the circulating theories on social media linking the barrage of outages.

"There is no conspiracy here," he told the BBC.

"There is something more ordinary, and more important to understand: the infrastructure that runs the world is changing faster than ever, and change is risk. Much of it is 30 to 40 years old, with decades of technical debt, and it's now being asked to change very quickly."

Beevers said AI is only part of the story.

"It's putting more strain on these legacy networks, and it's also creating real urgency around security," he said.

"Our customers are the amazing teams behind these networks at airlines, banking, energy, and retail who are essentially doing heart surgery on a global scale to get these networks back up and running quickly."

Vice President of Threat Intelligence for Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, Sherrod DeGrippo, said: "What this week really underscores is how tightly coupled, and fragile, our core digital infrastructure is, where a single software bug or router failure can cascade nationwide."

The French-made Falcon 6X replaces the ageing presidential jet, officials say

Ghana's government has defended its purchase of a new presidential jet amid criticism over its cost, as many citizens continue to struggle with the high cost of living.

The $60m (£46m) French-made Falcon 6X has sparked political row, with opposition politicians accusing President John Mahama's administration of misplaced priorities.

But the government says the purchase is justified, arguing that Ghana's improving economy makes the aircraft affordable and is needed to replace an ageing presidential jet.

The controversy comes as Mahama's administration seeks to demonstrate an economic recovery after years of financial difficulties that forced Ghana to seek IMF assistance.

Can Ghana's new president meet the voters' high expectations?

Manufactured by French aerospace company Dassault Aviation, the aircraft was delivered to the Ghana Air Force on Monday at a reported cost of $61m.

Parliament approved its purchase last December as part of a broader programme to modernise Ghana's military aviation fleet, which also includes four helicopters from Airbus.

The jet was welcomed with a water salute on Monday, but its arrival triggered criticism online and among opposition politicians over the cost and timing of the purchase.

While in opposition Mahama himself opposed buying a new presidential jet, prompting questions about why his administration has now gone head with the purchase.

Opposition MP Samuel Abu Jinapor questioned the government's priorities, saying the expenditure came at a time when many Ghanaians continue to struggle with the cost of living and youth unemployment remained alarmingly high.

"What was unacceptable in opposition cannot suddenly become acceptable in government merely because the occupants of power have changed," Jinapor added.

He accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of hypocrisy, recalling how its senior figures had strongly opposed proposals for a new presidential aircraft when they were in opposition.

Jinapor also called for greater transparency over the procurement process, how the purchase was financed and the government's justification for the expenditure.

Defence Minister Kenneth Adjei welcomed and inspected the new jet on Monday

The purchase has also prompted sharp criticism on social media, with some users arguing the money could have been spent on more pressing public needs.

"This money can employ over 100,000 nurses and 200,000 teachers," an X user posted.

But the government has rejected the criticism, saying Ghana's economic circumstances have changed considerably since the NDC opposed a similar purchase.

Peter Lanchene Toobu, chairman of parliament's Defence and Interior Committee, said the party had never opposed acquiring a presidential jet in principle.

Its objection, he said, had been on the timing when Ghana was experiencing severe economic difficulties.

"We agreed in principle that we needed to purchase a new presidential jet," he said.

He argued, however, that Ghan a could not justify the expenditure at a time when it was seeking a $3bn bailout from the IMF.

"The strength and macroeconomic stability of this country have enhanced our status in the sense that imports have become cheaper, and this is the right time," he added.

Toobu said the government had purchased the aircraft without borrowing, citing a stronger Ghanaian currency and improved economic conditions.

Government spokesperson Kwakye Ofosu also dismissed suggestions that the purchase was a misplaced priority.

He pointed to falling prices of construction materials and lower borrowing costs as evidence of the country's improved economic situation.

"When I was campaigning in 2024, and I was donating cement, it cost 115 cedis a bag. Today, for 80 cedis, you will get a bag of cement," he told JoyNews.

The controversy has also extended to the aircraft's interior, following claims that it has a dedicated bedroom and bathroom.

But Ofosu dismissed claims that the jet had such luxury facilities, saying the president has no intention of "bathing in the air".

"There certainly is no bathroom. President Mahama has no intention of bathing in the air," Ofosu said.

He explained that the jet has reclining seats that can be converted into sleeping arrangements but denied that it has a dedicated bedroom.

The government says the new jet will replace the 16-year-old Falcon 900EX, which has suffered recurring maintenance problems, including corrosion and leakages in its fuel tank.

The older jet was reportedly grounded in France for several months in 2025 while undergoing repairs.

Officials say the Falcon 6X has a longer flying range, reducing the need for refuelling stops on international trips and improving the reliability of presidential travel.

Harry Styles will compete with Cher for the weekend's most flamboyant outfit

Harry Styles will make his Glastonbury festival debut next year as one of the event's headliners, alongside Sam Fender and Billie Eilish - with Cher among the other stars on the bill.

Aged between 24 and 32, the trio represent the festival's youngest set of Pyramid Stage headliners since 1997.

Veteran pop icon Cher will play the coveted Sunday afternoon "legends" slot, which is often considered a fourth headline set. It will be her only UK festival appearance of the year.

Other acts on the line-up include Sombr, Sienna Spiro, Lily Allen, The Streets, Chase & Status, Kacey Musgraves, Primal Scream and breakout pop star Adéla.

Cher is bound to draw a huge crowd to hear hits like Turn Back Time, Believe and I Got You Babe

Electro pioneers Kraftwerk will make their Glastonbury debut with a headline set at West Holts - the festival's third-largest stage.

The event will also welcome experimental Canadian band Angine de Poitrine, who have drawn attention for their prog-rock sound and polka-dotted stage costumes; rap legends De La Soul and Mike D; and pop provocateur FKA Twigs.

Tickets for the festival sold out in just 42 minutes last month , with prices at an all-time high of £408, including a £5 booking fee per ticket.

Demand was particularly high after the event took a year off in 2026, allowing the fields at Worthy Farm in Somerset respite from the annual influx of 200,000 fans.

"We are so happy to be coming back after our fallow year and, as we head into winter after that peaceful period, we wanted to give you an early musical taster of what's to come at Glastonbury 2027 with this spread of incredible artists," said organiser Emily Eavis.

"We can't wait to see you down here on Worthy Farm in June for some much-needed good times!"

Gates will open on Wednesday 23 June; with music on the main stages kicking off on Friday 25 June.

Festival organiser Emily Eavis watched Sam Fender's set from the side of the stage in 2022

Sam Fender will headline the first night, in what will be his second appearance at the festival.

He last played in 2022, immediately before Billie Eilish, and fought back tears as thousands of fans chanted along to hits like Seventeen Going Under and Hypersonic Missiles.

"Me and the boys have never been here before," he said. "We've never been here as punters, never played here before and we're doing that all in one day, which is the most crazy experience."

He will return as one of the UK's biggest rock stars, having won the Mercury Prize for his third album, People Watching, in 2025. Earlier this year, his duet with Olivia Dean - Rein Me In - became the UK's longest-running number one single of all time.

Fender is expected to release a new album ahead of his Glastonbury slot, which will land in the middle of his catchily-titled Proper Massive Stadium Tour.

Billie Eilish was the youngest solo act to headline Glastonbury when she topped the bill in 2022

Harry Styles will take the Pyramid Stage crown on the Saturday.

It comes amid acclaim for his euphoric and athletic Together Together tour, which largely focuses on the understated dance anthems of his fourth album Kiss All The Time. Disco Occasionally.

The pop star has previously been spotted partying at the festival's late-night dance arenas, despite attempting to go incognito in tracksuits and sunglasses.

In 2022, he was rumoured to be making a guest appearance during Eilish's set after his music was played during an early-morning soundcheck - but the duet never materialised.

Instead, Eilish gave a universally well-received performance, described as "imperious [and] hugely engaging" by the Guardian, , external and "proof that the future is here" by the NME , external .

At the time, she was 20 years old - making her the youngest-ever solo act to headline Glastonbury.

Cher, meanwhile, will be the oldest ever act to play the legend slot - strutting through the gates of Worthy Farm at the age of 81.

The diva's appearance will come eight years after her last UK tour, and 63 years into a career that began with her ex-husband Sonny Bono, and recording sessions with Phil Spector's legendary Wrecking Crew band.

She emerged as a solo artist in the 1970s, scoring three US number ones, before switching into disco mode with Take Me Home.

In the 1980s, she became an award-winning actress and scored chart hits with FM rock staples like Turn Back Time and Just Like Jesse James.

Then in 1998, she revitalised her career with club anthem Believe, which helped to popularise the use of autotune in dance music.

Inducted to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2024, she is about to release the second volume of her memoir.

She has previously talked about retiring from live performance - but it seems the lure of Glastonbury was too tempting to turn down.

Cher will follow previous bookings in the crowd-pleasing legends slot including Sir Rod Stewart, Shania Twain, Diana Ross and Kylie Minogue.

More details about the 2027 line-up will be revealed in the New Year. Eavis has previously dismissed rumours that Madonna and Oasis will feature on the bill.

BBC comedy Ann Droid explored the possibility of a human (played by Sue Johnston) having an AI robot as a live-in carer (Diane Morgan)

"Human" is the Cambridge Dictionary's Word of the Year — defined as "having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines".

"The growth of AI means it is now necessary to explicitly say 'human' for things that once could only be done by humans," said chief editor Colin McIntosh.

Examples of current usage included actors Scarlett Johansson challenging "an assault on human creativity" and Matthew McConaughey protecting himself against unauthorised digital reproduction of his voice or image.

"The measure of AI's success should be how much it improves human lives," said Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates on learning about the dictionary's choice.

McIntosh said dictionary editors had to be on top of how words could change over time "to reflect what people say and what they write".

His research revealed a four-fold use of the word human since 1900.

"'Man' used to be used in this sense a lot more, but now it is not acceptable to use 'man' to mean men and women," he added.

"Human didn't come into use in Middle English until the 14th Century, from a French word. Shakespeare used it, but after that it was very restricted in use."

There had also been an increased use of compound words such as human-made and human-driven, to distinguish the works, qualities and skills of people from AI.

"Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking has made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI, from top mathematicians to teachers of young children," said McIntosh.

Oscar-winner Matthew McConaughey was the first actor to use trademark law to protect their likeness from AI misuse, according to his lawyers

Gates recently made the case for "human reserved jobs" , external , such as caregiving, and reiterated his call for a robot tax to help fund training for people who lose their jobs to AI.

Other examples included the Nobel Prize in Physics laureate Geoffrey Hinton, who has been described as the godfather of AI, who warned "we're creating alien beings. I'm willing to be selfish and choose humans".

Pope Leo XIV has spoken of new forms of "dehumanisation" , external and the "pressing duty to remain profoundly human".

"Right now our understanding of humanity is changing," said Dr Tom McClelland, a philosopher of science at the University of Cambridge.

"We're trying to understand the difference between a human mind and an artificial mind, between living beings like us and artificial beings that we're creating. What sets us apart? Is it consciousness, creativity or compassion?"

When we want to specify something is made by humans and not machines or AI, we now need to say it, said Colin McIntosh

In response to the surge in AI-created content , academics are hoping to develop a universally recognised symbol to denote something that is "human made", similar to the "Fairtrade" label that emerged in the 1980s.

Prof Rachel Adams, an expert on AI governance and human rights at the University of Cambridge, said: "AI brings us back to questions that we've asked for millennia — who are we? What does it mean to be human?

"AI is going to be a profound test for humanity. There's a real risk that it deepens existing inequalities, but it also has the potential to solve them."

Mauricio Pochettino became head coach of the USA men's national team in September 2024

Mauricio Pochettino has said he will restore Manchester United to being the most successful footballing side in the city.

The Argentine is scheduled to begin his new role as United manager on Wednesday after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract.

The United States beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati in his final game in charge on Tuesday, after which he spoke to TNT Sports. , external

Analyst DaMarcus Beasley, who spent the 2006-07 season on loan with Manchester City, joked that "Manchester is blue, it will always be blue".

Pochettino replied: "No way, you will see. Give me time and that is going to change."

The former Chelsea, Tottenham and Southampton boss is believed to have flown directly to Manchester on a private jet after the game.

"We're excited because the new challenge is big, but it's the adrenaline that you want to feel," he said.

"We are going to have a different job but we have the experience to deal with that. We need to add our common sense in the way that we are going to approach all the things.

"We know that it is not a situation that deserves to be at a club like Manchester United and for the fanbase."

Tuesday's win ensured the US advanced to the Concacaf Nations League semi-finals and that Pochettino finished with a 62.16% win ratio from 37 games in charge.

The 54-year-old led the team to the 2025 Gold Cup final and the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup, when the US were co-hosts.

"I am proud of what we achieved," he said in a statement on Instagram. , external

"When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team.

"This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally.

"Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

"I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves."

Littleham Brook in Exmouth turned blue following the pollution incident

People affected by a pollution incident that turned a brook bright blue are being asked to share their experiences as part of an ongoing investigation.

The Environment Agency has launched a survey following the contamination of Littleham Brook in Exmouth, Devon between 11 and 25 September .

It prompted warnings against swimming and other water activities at Exmouth beach while officials investigated the cause.

The survey , external closes on 18 December.

Clarissa Newell, regulatory manager at the Environment Agency, said: "We want information from people, businesses and organisations who may have been affected by this incident.

"This could be specifically during this period or you may still be experiencing ongoing impacts."

The Environment Agency said the anonymous feedback could help investigators understand the wider effects of the pollution and may lead to witness statements supporting the inquiry.

It said possible impacts included illness, cancelled water activities, disrupted visits and reduced income for businesses.

No information could be shared at this stage on the source of the pollution as it could affect any future legal action, it added.

Paper copies of the survey are available from Exmouth Town Hall.

From Spring 2027, under 16s will no longer be able to access several social media applications

More than 300,000 young people in Britain will work with researchers to help understand how the UK's forthcoming social media ban for under-16s could affect mental health.

The studies will examine the habits of the children and teenagers, including whether they spend less time on their phones and what they are replacing scrolling with.

Ten different projects have been commissioned, taking place across England, Wales and Scotland, to help reflect a diverse range of teenagers.

The social media ban, beginning in spring 2027, will follow a similar model to that already introduced in Australia to stop children accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.

Apps such as Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Snapchat and YouTube will be banned under new rules

The work, funded by health charity The Wellcome Trust, will help inform future online safety policies in the UK and internationally, with some early results available before the ban happens.

Researchers will use wearable technology, smartphones, digital diaries and surveys to collect data to see how young people respond to the ban, both physically and mentally.

And they will check whether young people find ways to circumvent restrictions.

Dr Camilla Iannone, research lead at Wellcome, said it was a once-in-a-generation opportunity to study at scale how social media and its restrictions affected youth mental health.

"We really don't think that this is a simple binary question of whether social media is good or bad, or whether restrictions work or don't work.

"Instead, the teams will study whether changing young people's digital environment leads to meaningful changes in their mental health and wellbeing."

Participants are being recruited to reflect a diverse range of young people, including different genders and sexual orientations.

People with existing mental health conditions, such as anxiety and depression, will also be included, as well as young people who are neurodivergent.

Groups have been set up at Cardiff University, the University of Oxford, the University of Birmingham, King's College London, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Manchester, the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, and University College London.

There have also been reports of Australian teens finding ways to get round the ban - with the UK government promising to make sure tougher blocks are in place.

Spanish police arrested Buchanan in Madrid

A British hacker has been sentenced to six years in a federal prison in the US for conspiring to hack into at least a dozen companies via text message phishing, and stealing over $11.6 million in cryptocurrency from individual victims.

24-year-old Tyler Buchanan started hacking as a teenager and was part of the collective of young hackers known as Scattered Spider, which has been blamed for a string of high profile cyber-crimes.

US prosecutors said the thefts had "severe, life-altering consequences" for victims and showed the growing threat posed by online crime groups.

The sentence brings to an end a years-long international investigation involving authorities in the UK, US, Spain and Canada.

Buchanan admitted taking part in a hacking campaign that began in 2021, when he was 19.

Working from his parents' home in Dundee, he and other English-speaking hackers in the US and UK targeted employees at major technology and telecommunications companies.

It made them $8m dollars in less than 2 years, according to US prosecutors.

Buchanan and his hacker gang sent out hundreds of SMS messages to the mobile phones of people who worked for large tech or telecoms companies.

The SMS phishing messages contained links to spoof websites designed to look like legitimate sites of victim companies.

The group used messages like "Hi, your account is due to expire - you need to log in to your work account here immediately or you will lose access to work apps".

The websites then lured the recipient into providing confidential information, including personal identifying information (PII), and account usernames and passwords.

The boys and young men did it on an industrial scale with Buchanan setting up a Telegram bot to collect all the victims' credentials as the duped workers unwittingly handed over their login details.

For some victim companies, subsequently stolen information included confidential work information, intellectual property, plus account access credentials, names, email addresses, and telephone numbers.

The group then used stolen information and SIM-swapping techniques to target cryptocurrency investors in the United States.

In the largest single theft, prosecutors said one victim lost $1.67m in December 2022.

Overall, authorities calculated that Buchanan and his co-conspirators stole more than $11.6m from victims.

Buchanan was also a victim of cyber-criminals.

In early 2023 his online identity and home address were leaked by rival hackers seeking access to his cryptocurrency.

Cyber security researchers and journalists reported that he was assaulted at his home and threatened with a blowtorch.

"TylerB and his group were highly sophisticated and organised but the violence he and others experienced was a sign of the troubling direction of these online communities of young hackers" says cyber security researcher Allison Nixon from Unit221B.

Buchanan then reportedly fled to Canada to escape further threats before returning home.

In April 2023, officers from Police Scotland searched Buchanan's bedroom after receiving a request from the FBI.

Investigators recovered a device containing the names and addresses of hacking victims, along with cryptocurrency seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim.

The following month, Buchanan left the UK again.

He was arrested on 31 May 2024 at Palma de Mallorca Airport in Spain while attempting to board a private flight to Naples.

After being extradited to the United States, he remained in custody before being sentenced this week.

In his November 2023 charge, Buchanan was named along with four American men and boys in their twenties and teens for alleged activity linked to the notorious cyber-criminal collective Scattered Spider.

They have all pleaded guilty too and are now serving time in jail.

Two other members of the Scattered Spider group were jailed in the UK in July for various cyber attacks including a disruptive one against Transport for London that caused £39m of damage.

‘Inteko y’Abaturage’, or Community Meeting, is seen here in Kamonyi district, souther of Kigali. Such gatherings are held across the country on a regular basis.

Imagine a child living with parents who struggle to provide food, decent housing and other basic needs. Neighbours know the family is struggling.

Under a new government mechanism, the child’s name could be discussed at a village assembly as a possible candidate for State guardianship.

But does this mean the Government can take children away from parents who are considered irresponsible or unable to care for them?

A new Ministerial Order governing State guardianship of children gives village assemblies the first role in identifying children who should be placed under the guardianship of the State.

Published in the Official Gazette on November 13, the order establishes a process that begins with the Village General Assembly.

It identifies the children and submits their names to the Sector, which assesses the list before forwarding it to the national institution responsible for children.

That institution validates the list before the guardianship is formally registered.

This is where the new rules leave important questions.

The order does not provide detailed criteria for selecting children. It does not explain whether the system targets abandoned children, those without parents or guardians, children experiencing neglect, or those living in extremely difficult conditions.

Nor does it say that poverty alone is sufficient reason to place a child under State guardianship.

The distinction matters. A child whose parents are alive and willing to raise them is not necessarily a child without a guardian. Article 119 of the 2024 Family Law provides for State guardianship of a child who has no guardian.

The new order does not expressly give village assemblies the power to remove children from parents simply because they are poor or considered irresponsible.

State guardianship does not automatically mean sending a child to an institution. Under Article 5, the District and the national child-protection authority first consider placing the child with a family willing to care for them.

A children’s welfare centre is an option if no family is willing.

The Central Government is also required to support families and centres financially where necessary, while Districts must monitor the children’s welfare and health and report every three months.

Parents who wish to resume guardianship of a child previously placed under State guardianship can apply through the District. The national authority assesses the application and communicates its decision within 30 days.

The biggest unanswered question remains how a village decides that a particular child should enter this system. The order does not spell out the evidence required, whether parents must be heard or whether a family should first be offered support.

The mechanism could help identify children who genuinely need protection. But clear rules will be essential to ensure that protecting vulnerable children does not become a reason for separating families simply because they are poor.

Mata celebrates winning Euro 2012 with Spain

Former Spain midfielder Juan Mata has announced his retirement from playing at the age of 38.

Mata, who made 41 international appearances, was part of the Spain squad that won the 2010 World Cup, and he helped his country win the European Championship two years later when he scored in the 4-0 final victory against Italy.

A former Real Madrid youth player, he joined Valencia in 2007 before a move to Chelsea in August 2011 where he won the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup.

Mata moved to Manchester United in January 2014 and helped them claim the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup prior to his departure in 2022.

He went on to have spells at Turkish side Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe in Japan before he played for Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory.

"Football will never leave my life," said Mata. "There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development.

"I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer."

Justin Devenny's equaliser in Budapest took Northern Ireland into Nations League A for the first time

Speaking before his side ground out the required point against Hungary to seal top spot in Nations League Group B2, Northern Ireland's Trai Hume told reporters that automatic promotion had not been the most immediate aim coming into the campaign.

Two years ago, this side were a League C team, battling to return to the second tier from a group containing Belarus, Bulgaria and Luxembourg.

Fast forward 24 months and a League A place was secured on the final night of an unbeaten campaign that had looked a serious challenge. Prior the trip to Georgia in September, Northern Ireland had a record of played 10, lost eight and drawn two at this level.

Across six games in eight weeks, the side won three and drew three, conceding just once along the way. Justin Devenny's brilliant equaliser in Budapest on Tuesday secured the draw required to top the group and earn promotion to the top tier for the first time.

"It's a great feeling for us," said manager Michael O'Neill.

"In a way, we sort of set out when we came into this level of competition first of all to try and stay in it. Obviously to do that, you have to, you have to be in the top two positions.

"We knew that would help us potentially with the draw for Euro 2028, but to come away unbeaten, to to finish top and to give the performances we've given against some very good teams, it's very encouraging."

Watch: Devenny the hero as NI earn promotion

Belief and bench help NI scale new heights

With such a young team on the international stage, there will always be more intangible markers of progress too.

It is perhaps easy to forget that not so long ago Pierce Charles' shot-stopping was being questioned as a weaker part of his game when compared to his range of passing.

Quite apart from a penalty save from Georgia's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to start the group, the Queens Park Rangers loanee made momentum-changing stops from Georges Mikautadze in Tbilisi and Danylo Sikan against Ukraine in Belfast last week.

All three of the Ruairi McConville-Tom Atcheson-Ciaron Brown defensive triumvirate have enhanced their reputations too, while, perhaps not yet in a first-choice XI, Patrick Kelly, Terry Devlin and Brodie Spencer feel increasingly trusted members of a deepening pool of players.

O'Neill may have only made nine changes to his starting teams across the six games, but it felt notable how often those coming in did not look out of place.

The bench then made a huge impact in the draw that sealed promotion with two players at opposing ends of the experience spectrum, Josh Magennis and Kieran Morrison, to the fore.

"We have a squad now where I think the younger players are coming in and making an impact straight away," said O'Neill, who still has the likes of Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard to come back into his squad.

"Which is a real positive, particularly if you look at the likes of Tom and Ruairi, but also Kieran Morrison and Ceadach [O'Neill] coming in and getting minutes early in their international careers.

"I just think that like the the squad is still very much still in development, we we still have areas where we still need to improve."

The next staging post for this Northern Ireland team is the Euro2 2028 qualifying draw in Belfast on 6 December.

They will be among the second seeds thanks to their top-two Nations League finish and, depending on whether they land in a four or five-team group, could face qualifiers as early as March next year.

"The great thing is we finish on a high and the players go back to their clubs now, they have to deal with a lot of football, they're all playing and demanding leagues," added O'Neill.

"Depending on the draw, we might come in in March and have friendly games which might be a nice thing for us to have.

"But we can just go in and see what the draw brings in December and then we can sort of plot the next 12 months."

After a string of impressive performances in the past three months, they will do so with serious momentum.

Bordeaux fans protested when the club were demoted to the sixth tier

The latest stop on Zinedine Zidane's homecoming tour was an important one for the new France head coach. When Les Bleus took on Turkey in Bordeaux on Sunday night, the ex-midfielder was returning to the city in which he spent four formative years of his playing career, between 1992 and 1996.

"I became a man in Bordeaux," Zidane fondly recalled in the build-up. France edged triumphed 2-1 with an uninspiring display, but it did not dampen the mood of the 40,000 fans inside the Stade Atlantique.

While the 1998 World Cup winner was not necessarily in familiar surroundings (the out-of-town stadium was built for Euro 2016, 20 years after his departure for Juventus), locals made every effort to make him feel at home, holding up a commemorative tifo before kick-off and chanting Zizou's name throughout.

Just a few miles up the road earlier that afternoon, Zidane's former club were playing their fifth match of the season in the sixth-tier Regional 1, in a north-western suburb of the city.

Thousands of Bordeaux fans had made the short away outing to Saint-Medard-en-Jalles' 3000-seater ground to watch their team seal a fifth win in five this season.

Girondins de Bordeaux, the six-time French champions, who were once regulars in European cups, now find themselves facing amateur opposition on a weekly basis.

Since 2022, the club has plummeted from Ligue 1 to the sixth tier through a combination of on-pitch struggles, mismanagement at all levels, and sanctions due to their financial troubles.

Listen to the latest Football Daily podcast

The club was taken over in 2021 by Gerard Lopez, who was previously in charge of Formula 1's Lotus as well as another French side, Lille.

While Bordeaux were already hamstrung by debts at that point, the situation on and off the pitch worsened under the Spanish-Luxembourgish businessman as the men's first team finished rock bottom of Ligue 1 in his first season.

A couple of seasons in Ligue 2 followed, before the club was docked down to the fourth tier in 2024. In their first National 2 season, they notably signed Andy Carroll but ultimately missed out on promotion.

The following campaign saw a repeat of that near miss, and the club was expelled from national-level football altogether this summer over their finances.

With Bordeaux left on the brink and whittled down to just eight full-time employees (down from around 250 a few years beforehand), Lopez sold up to Park Bench, a group of mainly British USA-based investors who also own Scottish side Dunfermline as well as a minority stake in Spanish second tier side Cordoba.

The supporters turned out in their numbers for the first home match of the campaign, which had been delayed amid the uncertainty over whether the club could continue running, against Stade Montois.

More than 11,000 tickets sold, a record crowd for that level of French football.

"140 years of history, we won't be stopped," read one of the banners held up by the Ultramarines fan group, who also made it a point to thank the seven first-team players who had stayed despite the club's double relegation.

The team is centred around a core of players with Ligue 1 and Ligue 2 experience. Steve Shamal, who scored a hat-trick in that 4-1 victory over Stade Montois, previously turned out for the likes of Caen and Annecy in the second tier.

"We know we should be higher up, but that certainty can also be a trap," said Shamal after the game. "We shouldn't think that it's going to be easy.

"We need to respect our opponents if we're going to put in good performances."

As the sixth tier of French football is regionalised, only the league winner in the Nouvelle Aquitaine region's top flight will earn promotion.

Their on-pitch success so far this season comes as little surprise given the gulf in quality compared to the rest of the league. Over the summer, Bordeaux notably managed to hold on to Europa League-winning full-back Almamy Toure, while former Belgian youth international striker Baptiste Guillaume also joined.

Several former players have also looked to get involved in Bordeaux's revival.

Benoit Tremoulinas, the former French international who was a part of the title-winning squad in 2008-09, notably announced that at the age of 40 he would be lacing up his boots again seven years after injury forced him to retire.

Paul Baysse, the former centre-back, is an assistant to head coach Arnaud Cormier.

Benoit Tremoulinas spent six years at Bordeaux, winning a league title and two cups, before also twice winning the Europa League with Sevilla

Perhaps the most significant endorsement the new owners could have hoped for was that of Alain Giresse, widely regarded as the club's greatest player. The Euro 1984 winner, who won three league titles while playing more than 500 times for the Marine et Blanc, was in attendance for the match against Stade Montois. He took the ceremonial kick-off before giving a full-time dressing room speech.

The new management unveiled their long-term plans for the club on Monday at Le Haillan, the city-owned training ground which includes a chateau that hosts the club's headquarters.

"We are humbled to have this responsibility," Park Bench investor Jeremy Green said.

"The club doesn't belong to Park Bench, it belongs to Bordeaux, it belongs to the 11,000 people who came to watch a Regional 1 game, to the players and to the community. We have a responsibility to rebuild this club.

"Our commitment to the community and to the players is that we will be fiscally responsible and patient.

"We're not a financial institution, we're a collection of individuals who bring with them business, sporting, analytical, and entrepreneurship skills."

Dominique Delport, the club's new president, revealed he knew Green and Twining through his wife, who studied at Oxford with them.

"We can learn from the club's golden years," the former journalist and advertising executive told BBC Sport, before adding that he would look to bring club legends to every league game.

Bordeaux won the Coupe de France as recently as 2013

While the club was sold for a symbolic euro, it did involve taking on long-standing debts which spanned transfer fees, stadium rent, and a compensation claim by former head coach Vladimir Petkovic.

Last Friday, the city's commercial court approved a request to restructure the debt as part of the club's continuation plan.

When Bordeaux were expelled from national-level football by the French FA at the start of the summer, the club used several avenues to appeal while the takeover was being finalised.

"We thought we had acquired the club in National 1 [the fourth tier]," Green and co-investor James Twining, told BBC Sport.

"Initially we walked away, but we were encouraged to come back," Green added. "We established that we were going to be able to restructure things and make it work.

"People around the club and in the local community encouraged us to try to find a way."

The six-time French champions have a long way to go before returning to the top flight.

"We're committing to a sensible financial structure, to a well-run club, and we're talking about 10 years to get this club back to Ligue 1," the new investors added.

A crucial step towards that long-term goal will be returning to the professional leagues, which would allow them to re-open the youth academy they were made to close when they dropped down.

Rebuilding the women's team, who were involved in the Champions League only a few seasons ago, is another one of the new owners' objectives.

Keeping the fans onside throughout the process will also be key, not least after the rift that opened up between groups during the previous ownership.

In any case, if the record-breaking turnout for Bordeaux's return to league action is anything to go by, their support seems unlikely to waver anytime soon.

Four members of Matos' coaching staff - Diogo Medeiros, Toze Mendes, Goncalo Ricca and head of goalkeeping Pedro Pereira – are also set to depart.

Radio 4 presenter Emma Barnett has hosted her final episode of BBC Radio 4's Today programme ahead of joining a new BBC show next year.

She used her final moments on the programme to praise "decent journalism and journalists" - citing those at the Times, Sunday Times and Guardian who worked on investigations into Russell Brand and David Walliams respectively.

Rwanda’s dramatic landscapes, winding mountain roads and breathtaking natural attractions could soon find themselves in the spotlight of one of the world’s most celebrated film franchises, following a proposal by the British Embassy in Kigali to have scenes of the next James Bond movie shot in the country.

The proposal places particular attention on Volcanoes National Park, home to the endangered mountain gorillas and some of Africa’s most spectacular volcanic scenery, alongside the picturesque shores of Lake Kivu and the winding roads of Musanze.

But beyond the beauty of these destinations, the suggestion points to an opportunity to position Rwanda as a competitive destination for international film productions, using its natural attractions to reach audiences far beyond its borders.

Volcanoes National Park, located in the northwestern part of the country, offers a distinctive cinematic environment.

Its chain of volcanic mountains, thick bamboo forests, mist-covered slopes and dramatic high-altitude landscapes provide the kind of atmosphere that could easily complement the visual identity of a James Bond production.

The park is part of the Virunga Massif, a transboundary mountain range shared by Rwanda, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Its rugged terrain and spectacular scenery could provide a compelling backdrop for scenes involving wilderness exploration, high-stakes encounters or dramatic pursuits.

The surrounding Musanze area also offers another attractive dimension. Its winding roads, steep hills and changing landscapes could provide an unusual setting for the franchise’s famous action sequences, particularly those involving high-performance vehicles and scenic driving routes.

Lake Kivu, meanwhile, could offer a completely different cinematic atmosphere, with its expansive waters, islands and beautiful lakeside scenery providing opportunities for scenes that capture the country’s more relaxed but equally captivating side.

Beyond the movie: An opportunity for tourism

The suggestion comes at a time when countries are increasingly recognising the power of international cinema in promoting tourism.

Films watched by millions of people can turn previously unfamiliar destinations into sought-after travel locations, creating what is commonly known as film-induced tourism.

For Rwanda, having its landscapes featured in a globally recognised franchise such as James Bond could generate international visibility that conventional tourism campaigns might struggle to achieve on the same scale.

The franchise, known for filming in visually striking destinations across different continents, has historically helped bring international attention to locations used in its productions.

A production in Rwanda could therefore create opportunities for tourism operators, hotels, transport companies, local creatives and other businesses connected to the visitor economy.

It could also strengthen the country’s ambitions to attract international film productions, develop its creative industry and promote its identity beyond traditional tourism marketing.

However, the British Embassy’s proposal should not be mistaken for confirmation that the next James Bond film will be produced in Rwanda.

No production agreement or filming schedule has been announced in the information available.

For now, the idea presents an intriguing possibility: that the mist-covered mountains of Volcanoes National Park, the winding roads of Musanze and the shores of Lake Kivu could become part of the cinematic world of James Bond, introducing the country’s spectacular landscapes to an entirely new global audience.

If the proposal eventually materialises, Rwanda would not simply be providing a beautiful filming location; it would be putting its natural heritage on the big screen for millions of potential visitors to discover.

President Paul Kagame joined thousands of football supporters at Amahoro Stadium in Kigali as the national football team, Amavubi, faced Mali in a crucial 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying encounter.

The return-leg fixture, played on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, attracted a massive home crowd, with supporters filling the stadium to rally behind the national team in its quest to secure a positive result against one of the strongest sides in Group K.

However, the visitors took the lead, leaving the home crowd anxious as Mali moved ahead 2-0.

The goal put additional pressure on Stephen Constantine’s men, who entered the encounter seeking redemption after suffering a narrow 3-2 defeat to the same opponents in Bamako on November 13.

In that first meeting, Amavubi demonstrated their attacking potential by taking the lead twice through Jojea Kwizera and Phanuel Kavita, only for Mali to fight back and claim all three points.

The return fixture in Kigali was therefore an important opportunity for the home side to respond, strengthen its position in Group K and keep its qualification ambitions alive.

Mali had won all three of its opening qualifying matches, collecting nine points, while Amavubi started the encounter with six points.

With thousands of supporters, including the Head of State, behind them at Amahoro Stadium, the national team was under pressure to turn the home advantage into a result.

Rwanda and Austria are seeking to strengthen their bilateral relations and explore new opportunities for cooperation following a meeting between senior government officials held in Vienna, Austria.

The Minister of State in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Dr Usta Kaitesi, held discussions with Sepp Schellhorn, Austria’s State Secretary at the Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs, on the sidelines of the 11th Vienna Migration Conference (VMC).

The meeting provided an opportunity for the two countries to review their existing diplomatic relations and discuss ways of expanding cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

The engagement comes at a time when both countries are looking to deepen their diplomatic and economic partnerships, with existing areas of cooperation including development, trade and investment, innovation, tourism, cultural diplomacy and renewable energy.

Organised by the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD), the conference brings together government officials, policymakers and migration experts from Europe, Africa, Asia and the Middle East to discuss migration governance, international partnerships, refugee protection and labour mobility. Review scores for GTA 6 are a fairytale ending after years of development

After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.

Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?

According to the first reviews, it's a resounding yes.

Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100 , external - tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.

Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.

They have been effusive with their praise, with gaming website IGN , external branding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".

Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.

"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome," reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote , external , but he added "there are also nits to pick".

For The New York Times , external one of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.

Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.

But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.

Critics say the relationship between Jason and Lucia is central to the game

The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, with The Guardian , external describing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".

And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.

"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".

Writing for Forbes , external , Paul Tassi said: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".

The Washington Post , external said GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", while Bloomberg , external 's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.

"It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote. "There's nothing else like it.

"While playing this game, I often found myself wondering how it even exists."

Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (£760m).

GTA 6 is the most hotly anticipated videogame ever

The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.

And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.

It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.

The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.

The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.

Mu gihe itereni zitwaye amatoni ibihumbi vy'ubutare bw'umujumbu zivuye muri Repuburika ya Demokarasi ya Kongo (RDC) ziriko zirengana zihuta mu karere abamwo, Manuela Julia w'imyaka 20 ntiyiyumvira ivy'ubutare nkenerwa cane canke imitahe y'amamiriyaridi y'amadolari.

Ico yiyumvira gusa ni ukuntu yoshobora kwiyunguruza bitamugoye.

Iryo barabara ry'indaraye rica muri Catumbela, hafi y'igisagara ca Lobito, kiri ku nkengera y'ibahari Atlantike muri Angola.

Kuri Julia, iryo barabara ryatumye ingendo zizimbuka ziranoroha kuruta uko vyahora.

Agira ati: "Imbere yaho, nategerezwa gukoresha itagisi, kandi vyari bizimvye cane. Ubu ingendo zirazimbutse kandi ziroroshe kuruta."

Ariko rero, imigambi ijanye n'iryo barabara ry'indaraye irarenze kure cane ivy'ukworohereza abantu kwiyunguruza mu karere.

Ni igice c'umugambi w'umuhora uzwi nka "Lobito Corridor", ushigikiwe na Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika, ugamije gutuma iki gihugu kironka ubutare nkenerwa bwo muri Afrika, no guteza imbere ugufashanya mu vy'ubutunzi hagati y'ibihugu vyo muri ako karere. Washington yizigiye ko uwo mugambi uzofasha kuzana amahoro mu buseruko bwa RDC, ahamaze igihe harangwa intambara.

Biciye ku masezerano yashitsweko ahagarariwe na Perezida wa Amerika Donald Trump, RDC n'Urwanda vyiyemeje kurushiriza gukorana mu vy'ubutunzi, harimwo no gukorera mu muco mu bijanye n'ubutare, kuva ku kungene bucukurwa gushika bushike kw'isoko, hamwe no guteza imbere inyubako n'ibindi bikorwaremezo bihuza ibihugu vyo mu karere.

Umugambi wagutse utegekanya ko ivyo bikorwa vyohuzwa n'iryo barabara ry'indaraye, ritwara ubutare buvuye muri Afrika yo hagati bwerekeza ku masoko yo mu bihugu vyo mu Burengero riciye muri Angola, aho kubujana mu Buseruko bw'isi, cane cane mu Bushinwa, nk'uko ahanini bigenda muri iki gihe.

Icizere ni uko gutunganya neza urudandazwa rw'ubutare rugakorwa mu mategeko no guhamagara abanyamitahe muri ico gisata bishobora gufasha kugabanya urudandazwa rw'ubutare rwo mu kinywabi, rusanzwe rufasha imirwi yitwaje ibirwanisho kuronka uburyo ikoresha mu ntambara, rukanatuma hatigera haboneka ituze.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Ariko none, ibarabara ry'indaraye ryubatswe kugira ngo rifashe gushikana ubutare ku masoko yo hirya no hino kw'isi, rirashobora no kuzana amahoro n'iterambere?

Umuhora wa Lobito uhuza igice co mu bumanuko bwa RDC, kirimwo ubutare bwinshi, n'inkengera y'ibahari Atlantike muri Angola, biciye kw'ibarabara ry'indaraye rya Benguela no ku kivuko ca Lobito.

Akamaro k'uwo muhora kariko karongerekana uko igitigiri c'abarondera ubutare bw'umujumbu na cobalt kiguma kiduga. Ivyo, ahanini biterwa n'uko isi iriko irahinduka irondera gukoresha inguvu zidahumanya ikirere, kuko ubwo bwoko bubiri bw'ubutare budahara mu gukora ubwoko bwinshi bw'ibikoresho ntanganguvu.

Wellington Muzengeza, umusesanguzi w'ingorane za politike zishobora kugira ingaruka ku butunzi, akorera i Johannesburg, avuga ko igihe uwo mugambi uriko urashirirwa mu ngiro gihambaye cane.

Agira ati: "Ugukwiragiza umuyagankuba n'ukuntu isi iriko yimukira ku gukoresha umuyagankuba udahumanya ikirere vyatumye umujumbu, cobalt hamwe n'uruhererekane rw'ubutare bwizewe birushiriza kuba ngirakamaro".

RDC iri mu bihugu vya mbere kw'isi bicukurwamwo cobalt n'umujumbu, co kimwe n'igihugu kibanyi ca Zambia.

Amerika ibona ko uwo muhora ushobora kuyifasha kuronka aho ikura ubutare hatandukanye, kugira ngo igabanye kuguma yitura Ubushinwa, igihugu gifise ububasha bukomeye kw'isi bwo guhingura ubutare.

Amasezerano y'ugufashanya mu vya politike n'ubutunzi hagati ya Amerika na RDC ashira imbere inzira iva mu gisagara ca Sakania muri Kongo igashika i Lobito, kugira ngo ikoreshwe mu gushora ubutare mu mahanga. N'amasezerano yerekeye imigenderanire mu vy'ubutunzi hagati ya RDC n'Urwanda ategekanya ko ibikorwa remezo n'imigambi ijanye n'urudandazwa hagati y'ibihugu vyo muri ako karere bihuzwa n'uwo muhora.

Uwo mugambi umaze gushirwamwo imitahe irenga imiriyoni 750 z'amadolari ya Amerika, harimwo amahera yatanzwe n'ikigo ca Amerika kijejwe gutanga uburyo no gushigikira imigambi mu mahanga, hamwe n'Ibanki ijejwe iterambere muri Afrika y'ubumanuko. Ayo mahera azokoreshwa mu kunagura no gutunganya neza inzira z'indaraye, ibikoresho bifasha kuyobora itereni, hamwe no gutunganya itereni ubwazo.

Iryo barabara ry'indaraye ryubatswe mu 1902, igihe Angola yari ikoronijwe na Portugal. Mu ntango, ryari ryagenewe gutwara ibidandazwa n'ubutare buvuye muri Afrika yo hagati bija ku nkengera y'ibahari Atlantike. Inyuma y'imyaka myinshi ridahita neza kubera intambara y'imbere mu gihugu yabaye muri Angola, ryarasubiwemwo kandi risubira gukora neza mu 2015.

Amerika yatanguye kugira uruhara muri uwo mugambi mu gihe Joe Biden yari akiri Perezida, ariko n'ubutegetsi bwa Donald Trump bwashitse bubandanirizako.

Ku kivuko ca Lobito cagenewe kwakira ubutare, imigambi mishasha ijanye n'uwo muhora iramaze kwibonekeza.

Igihe umurwi wa BBC wagendera ico kivuko, hari hahejeje gushika igariyamoshi yari itwaye amatoni agera ku 12.000 vy'ibikoresho bihingurwa mu butare bw'umujumbu bizwi nka "cathodes de cuivre", ivuye muri RDC.

Abakozi bapakuruye muri yo, ivyo vyuma babishira mu bubiko imbere y'uko bishirwa mu bwato bubijana kw'isoko mpuzamakungu, ahanini muri Amerika.

Uwo muzigo utunganywa n'ishirahamwe Lobito Atlantic Railway (LAR), rifise amasezerano y'imyaka 30 yo gutwara imizigo biciye kuri uwo muhora no gucungera ikivuko cagenewe kwakira ubutare.

Umuyobozi ajejwe ibikorwa vy'ishirahamwe Lobito Atlantic Railway (LAR), Nicholas Gregoir, avuga ko kuva iryo shirahamwe ritanguye gucungera ibikorwa vy'iyo nzira muri Nzero (1) 2024, igitigiri c'imizigo itwarwa n'amatereni cirwije n'incuro zibiri.

Imbere y'uko uno mwaka urangira, LAR iteganya kuba yatwaye amatoni agera ku 200.000 y'umujumbu biciye muri uwo muhora.

Ku mashirahamwe acukura ubutare, iyo nzira y'indaraye ituma ashobora gushikana umwimbu wayo kw'isoko mpuzamakungu akoresheje inzira ngufi kuruta izindi.

Umuyobozi mukuru w'ikivuko ca Lobito, Kátila Vanessa Monteiro da Silva Neto, agira ati: "Umuhora wa Lobito ni yo nzira ya hafi kuruta izindi ishobora gukoreshwa na Zambiya hamwe na RDC kugira bishike kw'ibahari Atlantike."

Zambiya, igihugu ca kabiri muri Afrika mu bicukurwamwo ubutare bw'umujumbu bwinshi, na co nyene kiriko kirategura umugambi wo guhuza akarere ka Copperbelt, karwiriyemwo ubwo butare, n'ikivuko ca Lobito mu kwubaka ibarabara ry'indaraye ry'uburebure bw'ibirometero 830.

Ariko rero, kuronka inzira nziza kandi ngufi yo gushikana umwimbu kw'isoko mpuzamakungu ntibisigura ko ubwo nyene ubutunzi bw'igihugu buca butera imbere ku rugero rukomeye.

Wellington Muzengeza agira ati: "Kwinjira mu mugambi w'umuhora w'ubudandaji si co kimwe no gutangura guteza imbere inganda mu gihugu. Ikizokwerekana ko uwo mugambi hari ico umaze si ukumenya gusa ko Zambiya ironse iyindi nzira ishobora kuyishikana ku kiyaga. Ahubwo ni ukumenya nimba iyo nzira izofasha mu guteza imbere ubutunzi kuruta uko bwari busanzwe."

Bamwe mu banya Angola bemera ko akamaro kanini k'iyo nzira y'indaraye gashobora kutagarukira gusa ku bikorwa vyo gucukura ubutare, ahubwo ko gashobora no kugaragarira mu vyo izofasha abadandaza n'abanyagihugu bo mu turere icamwo.

Umudandaza Adérito Areias agira ati: "Jewe ndawita umuhora w'iterambere."

Iyo nzira y'indaraye ica mu turere tumwe tumwe two muri Angola turangurirwamwo ibikorwa vyinshi vy'uburimyi.

Inzira nziza zo kwunguruza abantu n'ibintu zishobora gufasha abarimyi gushikana umwimbu wabo ku masoko manini no kugabanya umwimbu upfa ubusa.

Areias agira ati: "Iyo ata nzira ihari ikura umwimbu mu turere two hagati mu gihugu iwujana aho ukenewe, uca upfira aho wimburiwe."

Ariko rero, urugamba nyamukuru ni ugushira mu ngiro iyo ntumbero.

Mu mwaka wa 2025, ikivuko ca Lobito cakiriye congera kirungika imizigo ingana n'amatoni miliyoni 1.8. Muri iyo mizigo, amatoni agera ku 158.000 yari ay'ubutare. Ikibanza co kuri ico kivuko cagenewe kwakira imizigo gishobora kwakira amatoni ashika ku miliyoni 3.6 ku mwaka.

Neto avuga ati: "Ikivuko gisanzwe gifise ubushobozi bukwiye. Ico dukeneye ubu ni uko ibarabara ry'indaraye ryoba rifise ubushobozi buhagije bwo gutwara imizigo, hamwe n'ibindi bikoresho bikenerwa kugira amatereni ashobore gukora."

Ku banyagihugu baba mu turere iyo nzira icamwo, inyungu zayo zatanguye kwibonekeza ubwo nyene.

Ishirahamwe rya reta rishinzwe gutwara abantu n'ibintu kw'ibarabara ry'indaraye, Caminho de Ferro de Benguela (CFB), ritwara ingenzi, ryamenyesheje ko mu mwaka wa 2025 ryunguruje abantu imiliyoni 1.6, igitigiri kitari bwigere gishikwako.

LAR ivuga ko yahaye akazi abantu bashika hafi ku 1.000, aho 98 kw'ijana muri bo ari Abanya Angola.

Domingos Canhama, se w'abana bane akaba akora akazi ko gutwara imashini ziterura imizigo muri CFB, agira ati: "Aka kazi karamfasha kuronsa umuryango wanje ivyo ukeneye."

Yongerako ati: "Ndashobora kugaburira umuryango wanje, kubungabunga inzu tubamwo no gufasha dawe mu vyo akeneye."

Muzengeza avuga ko akaryo kanini kuruta gahagaze ku guteza imbere urudandazwa rwo muri utwo duce, hafatiwe ku bijanye n'ubuhinga bwo kwubaka no gutunganya ibikoresho, kubungabunga imashini n'ibindi bikoresho, gushingura imizigo hamwe no gutunganya umwimbu.

Ati: "Urudandazwa muri Angola rukeneye gushikira neza ibarabara ry'indaraye, aho kuba gusa hafi yaryo. Ivyo bisaba amabarabara matomato ashika kuri iyo ndaraye, umuyagankuba, ububiko bw'ibintu hamwe n'ibikorwa vy'ubwikorezi vyamaho buri gihe."

Ariko none, ubutare n'uburyo butwarwamwo biciye kw'ibarabara ry'indaraye vyoba bishobora gufasha kugarukana amahoro mu buseruko bwa RDC, aho intambara zo kurwanira ubutunzi bukomoka ku butare zimaze imyaka mirongo ziteza indyane?

Muri ibi bihe vya vuba, umuhari M23 urwanya reta ya Kongo warigaruriye uturere twinshi turwiriyemwo ubutare.

Reta ya Kongo ivuga ko igihugu kibanyi c'Urwanda ari co gifasha uwo muhari M23 kugira ngo gishobore gushikira ubutare buri ku butaka bwa RDC. N'ubwo hari ibimenyetso vyinshi vyerekana ko ivyo bishobora kuba ari vyo, Urwanda rurahakana ko rushigikira uwo muhari.

Amasezerano yashitsweko hagati y'Urwanda na RDC, yari ahagarariwe na Perezida Donald Trump, hagati ya RDC n'Urwanda, afise intumbero yo guteza imbere urudandazwa rw'ubutare rukorerwa mu muco, gushira imitahe ndengambibe muri iki gisata hamwe no kwubaka ibikorwa remezo bihuza akarere. Ivyo vyose bigamije kwirinda ko ubutare bw'ivyo bihugu bukoreshwa mu gufasha imihari yitwaje ibirwanisho.

Wellington Muzengeza, umusesanguzi ku ngorane zishobora guhungabanya ubutunzi, avuga ati: "Amerika ishaka kuronka ubutare nkenerwa mu vya gisirikare, mu vy'ubuhinga buhanitse hamwe n'umuyagankuba, mu gihe igerageza kugabanya ukwitura cane Ubushinwa bufise ijambo rikomeye."

Yongerako ati: "Ni co gituma umuhora wa Lobito urengeye kuba gusa ibarabara ry'indaraye. Ni igikorwa remezo gishobora guhindura inzira z'ubudandaji hamwe n'ububasha mu vy'ubudandaji.»

Mw'ikoraniro ryabereye i Paris muri Munyonyo(11), RDC yasavye Amerika gushira mu ngiro mu buryo bugaragara ubufatanye bw'ibihugu vyompi mu vy'iterambere, biciye mu gushora imitahe mu migambi ifatika. Yavuze ko intambwe izoba yatewe ikwiye gusuzumwa hisunzwe imigambi yamaze kurangurwa, aho gushingira gusa ku masezerano yashizweko umukono.

Umushikiranganji w'ubutunzi wa RDC, Daniel Mukoko Samba, yagize ati: "Dushaka ko aya masezerano afasha mu guhingurira ubutare imbere mu gihugu, atume imiryango n'amashirahamwe baronka umuyagankuba, hamwe no kugarukana amahoro mu buseruko bw'igihugu."

N'ubwo ubutare bwinshi bwotangura gucuruzwa biciye mu nzira zemewe n'amategeko, ibikorwa remezo vyiza vyonyene ntivyotorera umuti amatati ya politike n'ay'umutekano ari mu bituma iyo ntambara ibandanya.

Hari kandi ikibazo c'ababitungiramwo. Igice kinini c'ubutare bw'umujumbu muri RDC, biciye i Lobito, kijanwa gutunganirizwa hanze ya Afrika.

Angola irashobora kuronka amahera biciye mu kwemerera imizigo guca ku butaka bwayo, hamwe no guha abantu akazi mu bijanye no gutwara no gucungera imizigo. Ariko ibikorwa vyinshi bituma ubwo butare bwongerwa agaciro kurushiriza bikorerwa mu bindi bihugu.

Umushikiranganji ajejwe imigenderanire ya Angola n'ayandi makungu, Téte António, yabwiye BBC ati: "Iyo ushoye hanze y'igihugu ibidahinguye, uba kandi ushoye hanze y'igihugu akazi n'ubumenyi bijanye."

Areias na we nyene aratewe umutima uhagaze n'ico kibazo.

Ariko arerekana ko ibihugu bikwiye gushira imbere guteza imbere uguhingurira imbere mu gihugu, yagize ati: "Ntitwari dukwiye gushora hanze ya Afrika lithium, ahubwo dukwiye gushora amabateri".

Dusubiye i Catumbela, ibiganiro nk'ivyo bishobora gusa n'ibiri kure y'ubuzima bwa misi yose bw'abanyagihugu.

Kuri Julia, iyo nzira y'indarayi isanzwe imufasha kwiyunguruza ku mahera make kandi bitamugoye.

Ariko, kugira ngo uwo mugambi werekane ko washitse ku ntumbero, bizovana n'uko uzoshobora gukora ibirenze kwihutisha gusa ugutwara ubutare ku masoko mpuzamakungu.

Ikibazo gihambaye kuruta ibindi ni ukumenya nimba uwo muhora ushobora no gufasha mu kugarukana amahoro arama mu buseruko bwa RDC, aho ubwo butare bucukurwa.
